observations.seen: Frame 1 has a warm sun glow in the upper right and soft fill. Frame 2 is evenly lit with almost no contrast on the fairway. Frame 4's night key is a hard white light on teal grass, with no falloff or local light sources.

Golfer and cart shadows read in frames 1 and 4. Frame 4's golfer shadow is sharp, but the trees cast weak or absent contact shadows in frames 2 and 3, and the long tree shadows in frame 1 are faint bands.
The club shaft and head show no environment reflection. The white golf cart in frame 1 is a flat matte white with no specular response to the sky.
The fairways are vast empty planes that run to a hard horizon. Frame 3 is a featureless brown dirt plain with tiny cone props, and frame 4's sky is a flat navy fill with no gradient, moon or stars.
Frame 1 has mild distance haze. Frame 3 has floating orange ember particles. Frames 2 and 4 have almost no aerial perspective, so the horizon line is crisp and the scale reads small.

The grass is a visibly repeating tiled texture. Frame 3's ground uses an obvious hex-cobble tile that looks like a placeholder. The trees are untextured smooth spheres, and the tee markers are plain red boxes.
The trees are stacked-sphere primitives and the background props are tiny cones. The golfers are low-detail rigged figures with stiff hands. The cart in frame 1 is the most detailed asset in the set.
In frames 2 to 4 the golfer is pushed to the far left edge and a second figure is cropped by the frame. The center is empty grass, and the white aim line is the only element leading the eye.
The camera is a low third-person view behind the tee, not the orthographic 70° broadcast view the recipe expects. Framing of the subject changes between frame 1 and frames 2 to 4.
Frame 1 has mild bloom and a filmic tone. The other frames look flat and over-saturated (frame 2) or muddy (frame 3), with no visible color grading consistency or vignette.

Frame 1 has a clean dark HUD panel with hole, strokes, score, wind and club readouts, plus a gradient power bar. The bottom control strip and the '52%' label are tiny and low contrast. Frames 2 to 4 show no HUD.
